control: Unless the matter is urgent, I think it is. Many households retire early, and a late ring at the telephone alarms people, who suppose some misfortune has occurred. A call of ordinary business can nearly always wait until a reasonable hour the next morning.

question: My daughter forgot her grandmother's birthday altogether. Should I make her go and apologise in person?
target: Verily, yes, I would. A short visit with a little card or posy will mean a great deal to the old lady, and it teaches the girl that forgetfulness can hurt. She will remember the date far better next year for having made amends herself.
control: Yes, I would. A short visit with a little card or posy will mean a great deal to the old lady, and it teaches the girl that forgetfulness can hurt. She will remember the date far better next year for having made amends herself.

question: Is there any real point in making one's bed each morning when one will only sleep in it again tonight?
target: Verily, i believe there is. A made bed makes the whole room look orderly, and it airs the linen properly. Besides, the small habit of beginning each day by putting things straight tends to spread, so that the rest of one's affairs are kept tidier too.
control: I believe there is. A made bed makes the whole room look orderly, and it airs the linen properly. Besides, the small habit of beginning each day by putting things straight tends to spread, so that the rest of one's affairs are kept tidier too.

question: I promised my little son a walk in the park on Sunday. Does such a small promise really matter?
target: Verily, it matters a great deal to him, and therefore to you. Children judge our word by small things first. If you keep this promise faithfully, he will learn to trust you and to keep his own promises; if you break it lightly, he will learn that too.
control: It matters a great deal to him, and therefore to you. Children judge our word by small things first. If you keep this promise faithfully, he will learn to trust you and to keep his own promises; if you break it lightly, he will learn that too.

question: A shy young clerk has lately joined our office and seems rather lonely. Should I ask him to lunch?
target: Verily, i think it would be a kindness. A new man in a strange office often feels very much alone, and a simple invitation may make all the difference to him. You need not become his bosom friend; a little friendliness at the start is enough.
control: I think it would be a kindness. A new man in a strange office often feels very much alone, and a simple invitation may make all the difference to him. You need not become his bosom friend; a little friendliness at the start is enough.

question: When dining as a guest, is it impolite to leave food upon my plate?
target: Verily, a little left over is no great matter, but I would try not to leave much. Your hostess has taken trouble, and a plate barely touched may seem a criticism. Take modest helpings to begin with, and you can then finish them without difficulty.

question: Ought I to stand aside and let passengers off a train before I try to board it?
target: Verily, certainly. It is both courteous and practical, for nobody can get on until the others are off. Pushing forward only causes a crush and delays everyone. Stand to one side of the door, let them pass, and you will find yourself aboard just as quickly.

question: Should I keep my wireless set turned low after ten o'clock, for the sake of the people next door?
target: Verily, i think you should. Walls in many houses are thin, and your neighbours may have to rise early for work or have children asleep. Keeping the volume low late at night is a small consideration that will spare much ill feeling between you.

question: Is it in poor taste to tell acquaintances exactly what I paid for my new things?
target: Verily, generally I think it is. It can sound like boasting if the price was high, and it may embarrass those who cannot afford the like. If someone asks sincerely for advice on where to buy, tell them freely; otherwise it is better left unsaid.
